One page for mid-operation checks.
For full details, read [textlink="AN/PRC-117G Radio" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] and [textlink="Field Headsets" link="AU14CommsHeadsets"].
## Talking
[bold]Key[/bold]
[bold]Use[/bold]
[color=#3FCF8E]:h[/color]
Headset default net.
[color=#3FCF8E]:v[/color], [color=#3FCF8E]:a[/color], etc.
Other keyed nets. Examine your headset to see its letters.
[color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color]
AN/PRC active net. Trained roles only.
[color=#3FCF8E]:x[/color]
Headset direct frequency. Tune the headset first.
Trained AN/PRC roles are RTO, Commander, Officer Adjutant and Advisor.
For CLF, the Cell Leader is trained.
## Range
Stock figures assume whip antenna and TX MED.
[bold]System[/bold]
[bold]Clean[/bold]
[bold]Weak or Lost[/bold]
Named net via relay
0 to 30 tiles from radio.
Garbled to 45. Dead past 45.
Direct frequency
0 to 30 tiles from speaker.
Garbled to 50. Dead past 50.
Direct frequency bridged
Both users within 50 tiles of the AN/PRC.
Fails if either user is outside bridge range.
Transmit power and antenna change these ranges.
## Antennas
[bold]Antenna[/bold]
[bold]Best Use[/bold]
[bold]Note[/bold]
[bold]WHIP[/bold]
Patrols and moving RTOs.
Stock range while moving or standing.
[bold]MAST[/bold]
Command posts and retrans stations.
About double range while stationary. About half stock range while moving.
Use the whip when moving.
Use the mast when the radio is planted or staying still.
## Operating Modes
[bold]Mode[/bold]
[bold]Use[/bold]
[bold]Good[/bold]
[bold]Bad[/bold]
[bold]FH[/bold]
Enemy EW or jamming.
Jamming reduced by 1 tier. Can transmit inside jam fields.
1.5x battery. Small DF signature even when secured.
[bold]SC[/bold]
Normal secured radio work.
0.75x battery. No DF signature while secured.
No jam resistance.
[bold]CT[/bold]
Command-only AN/PRC traffic.
Invisible to interceptors. No DF signature.
Only fill-loaded AN/PRCs decode it. No jam resistance.
[bold]PT[/bold]
Open broadcast or dying battery.
0.5x battery.
Readable by everyone. Jamming +1 tier. Worst DF risk.
Fill secures every mode except PT.
Quick rule: - FH under enemy EW. - SC when the air is quiet. - CT for command-only traffic. - PT when you accept that everyone can read it.

## Squelch
Squelch filters noise. Clean traffic still passes.
[bold]SQL[/bold]
[bold]Effect[/bold]
[bold]0[/bold]
Open. Lets all static through.
[bold]1[/bold]
Cuts heavy static and undecodable crypto.
[bold]2[/bold]
Cuts medium jammer garble.
[bold]3[/bold]
Default. Cuts jammer garble.
[bold]4[/bold]
Maximum. May cut weak edge-of-range signals.
If you only hear silence near a jammer, drop to SQL 2 or 1.
## COMSEC
[bold]Action[/bold]
[bold]Result[/bold]
Insert fill card
Secures faction nets, except PT.
[bold]ZEROIZE[/bold]
Ejects the card intact.
[bold]DESTROY[/bold]
Deletes the card when there is no time to save it.
[bold]RECRYPTO[/bold]
Makes all older faction cards stale, including captured ones.
Captured enemy card
Loads into your radio and decodes their net until they recrypto.
Replacement fill comes through normal supply.
## Staying Alive on the Net
DF risk, brightest first: - PT. - Faction net traffic without matching fill. - Secured FH.
Secured SC and CT have no DF signature.
Repeated open transmissions from one spot help enemy EW locate you.
Keep it short, move after sending, or go quiet for a minute to reset the risk.
[bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] reports which stations hear you clean or degraded.
Inside jamming, it also gives a bearing to the strongest emitter.
